items.followUp: What is meant by understanding a problem, and what information should be identified before solving it?

rubric.why: Careful analysis clarifies what the problem asks.
rubric.description: Explain that the problem must be analyzed.
rubric.how: State that understanding begins by carefully examining the problem.

rubric.why: Recognizing the information provided establishes what is available for solving the problem.
rubric.description: Identify the given information or input.
rubric.how: Mention the facts or input provided in the problem.

rubric.why: Knowing the required result clarifies what the solution must produce.
rubric.description: Identify the required result or output.
rubric.how: State what result or output is needed.

rubric.why: Conditions and constraints affect which solutions are acceptable.
rubric.how: Mention any limits or conditions the solution must follow.

modelAnswer: Understanding a problem means carefully analyzing it to know exactly what must be solved.
Identify the information given in the problem.
Determine the result or output that is required.
Note any conditions or constraints that the solution must follow.

items.followUp: Describe one advantage and one disadvantage of star topology.

rubric.why: A central connecting device is the defining feature of star topology.
rubric.description: Name the central hub or switch.
rubric.how: State that the devices connect to a central hub or switch.

rubric.why: This explains how devices are arranged around the central device.
rubric.description: Explain the individual connections to the central device.
rubric.how: Say that each device has its own link or connection to the central device.

rubric.why: Easy expansion or fault identification is a practical advantage of this arrangement.
rubric.description: Give an advantage of star topology.
rubric.how: Mention that adding a device or identifying a fault in a link is easy.

rubric.why: Failure of the central device can stop communication across the network.
rubric.description: Give a disadvantage of star topology.
rubric.how: Explain that failure of the hub or switch may stop network communication.

modelAnswer: In a star topology, every computer or device is connected to a central hub or switch.
Each device has its own link to this central device, which manages communication.
It is easy to add a device and to identify a fault in an individual link.
If the central hub or switch fails, communication across the network may stop.

items.followUp: How does data travel in a ring topology, and what may happen if a link breaks?

rubric.why: A closed loop is the defining arrangement of ring topology.
rubric.description: State that devices form a closed ring or loop.
rubric.how: Describe the connections as a closed path.

rubric.why: In a basic ring, each device connects to its two adjacent devices.
rubric.description: Explain that each device connects to two neighbours.
rubric.how: State that a device is linked to the device on either side.

rubric.why: This describes how data moves through the ring.
rubric.description: Explain that data passes from device to device around the ring.
rubric.how: Mention that data travels around the loop through the connected devices.

rubric.why: A failed device or broken link can interrupt communication in a basic ring.
rubric.description: State a limitation related to device or link failure.
rubric.how: Explain that a failure or break may disrupt network communication.

modelAnswer: In a ring topology, each device is connected to two neighbouring devices, forming a closed loop.
Data passes from one device to the next around the ring.
The devices cooperate to forward data along the ring to its destination.
A failed device or broken link can disrupt communication around the network.
